title: Matthias (Acts 1:15–26)
hook: they pray, cast lots, and the twelfth place is filled

segments.voice: Yesterday, the start of Acts, and the word witness. Your line was you shall be witnesses.

Every team photo with an empty spot has a story. A chair left empty at the table, a name missing from the roster. Someone has to decide whether to fill it, and how. After the Ascension the disciples go back to an upper room in Jerusalem and pray together, about a hundred and twenty of them, Luke says, with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus. There were twelve apostles. Now there are eleven. And Peter, only weeks after his own worst failure, stands up to deal with the empty chair.
screen: `AN EMPTY CHAIR.` → `A HUNDRED AND TWENTY IN PRAYER.` → `TWELVE, NOW ELEVEN.`

segments.voice: Peter speaks about Judas plainly and without gloating: he was numbered with us and had a share in this ministry. Then he gives the qualifications for the empty place. It has to be someone who was with them the whole time, from John's baptism to the day Jesus was taken up, someone who can be a witness with them of the resurrection. Yesterday's word, witness, as the job description. Two men fit: Joseph called Barsabas, also known as Justus, and Matthias. Both, we're told, were there from the start, and Acts tells us nothing more about either one. Then they do two things, in this order. First they pray, saying: Lord, you who know the hearts of all, show which of these two you have chosen. Then they cast lots, something like drawing straws. In the Douay-Rheims: "And they gave them lots, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles." Casting lots was an old way in Israel of leaving a decision to God; Proverbs says the lot is cast, but the decision is the Lord's. Some readers notice that once the Spirit comes at Pentecost, Acts shows the apostles deciding in other ways, by prayer, discussion and the Spirit's lead. What stays is the order: they prayed first. And Matthias, chosen by a falling lot, is honored by the Church as an apostle. Faithful from the beginning, and Acts never names him again.
screen: `THE EMPTY PLACE.` · `A WITNESS FROM THE START.` · `THEY PRAY, THEN CAST LOTS.` · `CHOSEN, THEN NEVER NAMED AGAIN.` · then, large: `MATTHIAS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a decision in front of you, large or small: a job, a conversation, a purchase, where to spend Saturday. Hold the options side by side, the way the apostles held two names, and don't decide yet; just breathe with them there together. If you pray, borrow the apostles' request in your own words, asking God, who knows the heart, to show you; if you don't, simply hold the options in quiet.
Matthias. Chosen after prayer and the casting of lots to take the twelfth place among the apostles. Today's word.
Your line: they prayed first. Prayer, then the choice, always in that order. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics keep a feast of Saint Matthias, Apostle, and the Church often begins important choices, like a papal conclave, with a Mass asking the Holy Spirit's guidance.

original.note: Greek: lot, also a share or portion; it gives English the word clergy.

what a scholar hears: klēros means both lot and share (Acts 1:17, 26) and is the root of 'clergy'; Proverbs 16:33 lies behind the practice.
